## 3.1.1 Monotherapy - Study TEMPO (Protocol 232)
This was a North American, multicenter (32 centers: 28 US and 4 Canadian centers), randomized, double-blind, parallel group, phase III clinical study conducted to early PD patients.

design.text: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group; 26-week placebo-controlled treatment phase followed by a 26-week active-treatment phase

population.text: Early Parkinson's disease patients not treated with levodopa at enrollment

citations.quote: Study TEMPO was conducted in early Parkinson's disease patients who were not treated with Levodopa (LD) at the enrollment.

endpoint.text: Change from baseline in the subtotal of UPDRS section III scores (ADL, Motor, and Mentation)

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint for the placebo-controlled phase was the change in subtotal of UPDRS section III scores (ADL, Motor, and Mentation) from baseline to the termination visit.

indication.text: Treatment of the signs and symptoms of idiopathic Parkinson's disease as initial monotherapy and as adjunct therapy to levodopa

citations.quote: AZILECT (rasagiline mesylate) is indicated for the treatment of the signs and symptoms of idiopathic Parkinson's disease as initial monotherapy and as adjunct therapy to levodopa.

target_moa.text: Irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase (MAO), inhibiting MAO type B, the major form in human brain that regulates metabolic degradation of catecholamines

citations.quote: AZILECT is an irreversible monoamine oxidase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of idiopathic Parkinson's disease. AZILECT inhibits MAO type B, but adequate studies to establish whether rasagiline is selective for MAO type B (MAO-B) in humans have not yet been conducted.
MAO regulates the metabolic degradation of catecholamines and serotonin in the CNS and peripheral tissues. MAO-B is the major form in the human brain.
AZILECT Tablets contain rasagiline (as the mesylate), a propargylamine-based drug indicated for the treatment of idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

key_safety.text: As monotherapy, most common AEs (≥5%, ≥1.5x placebo) were flu syndrome, arthralgia, depression, dyspepsia, and fall; e.g., arthralgia 7% vs 4%, flu syndrome 5% vs 1%. As adjunct to levodopa, dyskinesia 18% vs 10% placebo was most common. Serious class risks include hypertensive/tyramine reactions and drug interactions.

citations.quote: The most commonly observed adverse events that occurred in \ge 5\% of patients receiving AZILECT 1 mg as monotherapy (n=149) participating in the double-blind, placebo-controlled trial and that were at least 1.5 times the incidence in the placebo group (n=151), were flu syndrome, arthralgia, depression, dyspepsia, and fall.
